cards.title: Battle page: tiers
cards.text: Set any hero's tier from 0 to 3, field one kind at several ranks, bigger grounds, a dev unlock. Live as 0.14.1.
cards.why: Your list and your battle answers, built. A hero can now fight itself at another tier. Mark what's still clumsy.

parts.title: Hero tiers
parts.text: Yours is the hero as it is at camp. Tier 0 has nothing bought; tier 1 is the first shell of the web with every ability; tier 2 the second shell; tier 3 the whole web. Tap a hero's tag to change it.

parts.title: Add at a tier or rank
parts.text: The picker has an Add at / Add as row, so you can put in 2 major slimes, 1 plain and 3 elites, or a Paladin at tier 2 beside one at tier 3.

parts.title: Dev unlock
parts.text: A switch at the bottom of the picker fields every hero and monster, beaten or not.

parts.title: Strength switch
parts.text: By dungeon: a monster is as strong as on its own dungeon's first floor. Evened out: every monster as at the first dungeon, to compare kinds like for like.

parts.title: Bigger grounds
parts.text: Small, Large (the default now, nearly 3 times the old area) and Huge. The camera starts pulled back on the big ones; pinch to look closer.

parts.title: Setup and result layouts
parts.text: A stack is a row now, with its tag and count. The result is the verdict, then each side as a short list with a damage bar a kind, all to one scale.

cards.title: Wipes, and resting
cards.text: A wipe now loses 75% of the run's gold and nobody rests. Should resting go everywhere else too?
cards.why: You asked for the wipe change. Leaving early still costs 20% and still sends the hurt and downed to rest, which is now the only place resting exists.
cards.pick: Remove resting altogether: gold is the only price, 20% for leaving early and 75% for a wipe.

cards.title: New heroes falling behind
cards.text: A hero recruited late starts at level 1 beside a party at 40. You asked for suggestions.
cards.why: Levels only matter for skill points, so the gap is points. The fix should let a new hero catch up fast without making old heroes' levels feel wasted.

options.label: New recruits join near the party's level
Low heroes earn XP much faster
Pay gold at camp to train a hero up
Heroes left at camp earn part of the XP

cards.details:
Join near the level: a recruit arrives at three quarters of your highest hero's level, with the points to spend. Simplest, but buying a hero late is then as good as raising one.

Faster XP (my pick): a hero below your highest earns XP faster the further behind it is, up to four times, so it catches up in a handful of runs while being carried. Nothing is free and nothing new to learn.

Training: gold buys levels at camp up to your highest hero's. Gives gold a late use, but it's a menu, not play.

Bench XP: everyone at camp gets a third of what the party earns. Keeps the whole roster moving, but makes the party choice matter less.

cards.title: The trail's harsh cut
cards.text: Locked dungeons on the trail now fade in instead of starting at a hard line, and biomes blend into each other.
cards.why: You said the delve screen had a harsh cut. This is the one I found; if you meant another, comment with where.
